title: Does DMSA (succimer) lower lead or improve cognition, autism, or arsenicosis?

grade.title: At least one good randomized trial, or consistent human evidence from more than one source
grade.basis: One large randomized trial (TLC, n=780) showed lower blood lead.

answerHtml: In children with blood lead of 20 to 44 µg/dL, the TLC randomized trial found that succimer lowered blood lead and did not improve cognition, behavior, or neuropsychological scores. A Cochrane review of chelation for autism found only one randomized trial and no evidence of an effect on symptoms. One small randomized trial in chronic arsenicosis found no significant benefit versus placebo.

sections.heading: Studies
sections.html:
Human studies of DMSA in this corpus. Not a dosing guide.
StudyDesignResult
Rogan 2001 TLC RCT, placebo, 780 children aged 12 to 33 months, blood lead 20 to 44 µg/dL Lowered blood lead. No improvement in cognition, behavior, or neuropsychology at 36 months. Follow-up to age 7 also null. PMID 11346806.
Adams 2009 Open first round, then randomized rounds, children with autism Authors state the first round compromised the placebo comparison. PMID 19852789.
James 2015 Cochrane Systematic review, 1 RCT included No evidence that multiple rounds of oral DMSA affected autism symptoms. Authors: risks currently outweigh proven benefits. PMID 26114777.
Guha Mazumder 1998 Double-blind RCT, 11 versus 10 adults with chronic arsenicosis No significant clinical, biochemical, or histologic benefit versus placebo. PMID 9865236.
